D_CLIP2026_grouping_counterexample.question: How can grouping by bare video ID reverse the Raw/L2 AUC comparison when frame predictions are fixed?
D_CLIP2026_grouping_counterexample.claim: For the accepted mean-logit CLIP seed2026 counterexample, changed ID weights alone flip the Raw/L2 difference; subsequent group averaging partially offsets it.
D_CLIP2026_grouping_counterexample.a: Decomposition: two individually singleton-heavy methods receive much greater effective fake mass before group-score averaging.
D_CLIP2026_grouping_counterexample.b: Fixed-score evaluation intervention: trace L2-minus-Raw under original natural weights, equal-ID member weights, then equal-ID mean scores.
D_CLIP2026_grouping_counterexample.scope: One explicitly selected existence counterexample, not a five-seed/backbone robustness estimate. Source finite complete cohort:157real12037fake/1830collisionIDs.
D_CLIP2026_grouping_counterexample.uncertainty: No error bar: deterministic score comparisons from one model and fixed finite cohort. It is not an estimate of seed variation; target relation-bootstrap CI unavailable under frozen support rule.
